title: Sustained-tier micro-reset and fairness smoothing for reserved capacity
creator: Ava Marshall
description:
Problem: Reserved-tier customers with sustained, near-capacity traffic patterns experience periodic hard resets (monthly/daily/rolling epoch boundaries) that cause bursts of throttling and poor request-level fairness. This leads to support churn and noisy billing artifacts when tenants cross epoch boundaries or when their usage drifts across timezone/region cutovers.

Goal: Introduce a micro-reset + smoothing policy for reserved capacity slices that: (1) preserves global invariants (total reserved tokens per contract), (2) reduces cliff-like throttling on epoch boundaries, (3) enforces fairness between tenants sharing reserved pools and on-hosted fallbacks, and (4) is auditable and reversible for billing reconciliation. The change should be opt-in under a feature flag for dedicated pools and validated via canary tenants before broad rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic micro-reset algorithm is implemented that permits controlled small token replenishments mid-epoch without violating committed reserved capacity budgets.
No customer sees a net increase in billed tokens beyond their committed quota across a full billing epoch (end-to-end reconciliation test).
Latency impact under steady-state load < 2% p95 regression on serving paths.
Dashboard surfaces new metrics: micro-reset-rate, per-tenant-smoothing-offset, pool-fairness-index. Alerts fire if smoothing increases 95th percentile throttling for any tenant by >5%.
Feature gated: can enable per-pool and per-tenant; rolloutable via console and config API.

implementation_notes: Design summary: Each reserved tenant maintains a 'reservoir' R(t) that decays towards 0 with half-life H (configurable per-pool). Tokens consumed reduce R immediately. At configured micro-reset intervals (e.g., every 10 minutes), system may add micro-credits up to a per-interval cap C such that integrated micro-credits over billing epoch <= allowed carryover budget B. Carryover budget B computed from reserved contract parameters and customer opt-in level.

Pseudocode (simplified):
  on_request(tenant, tokens):
    if tenant.pool.reservoir >= tokens: serve and reservoir -= tokens
    else if fallback_allowed: route to hosted tier with fallback accounting
    else throttle

  reservoir_decay_worker: every minute:
    reservoir = reservoir * exp(-ln2 / H)

  micro_reset_worker: every 10m:
    add = min(C, max(0, B_remaining / intervals_remaining))
    reservoir = min(reservoir_cap, reservoir + add)
    record_metric("micro_reset.granted", add, tenant)

Accounting guarantees: ledger records micro-reset grants as 'deferred credits' with unique id. At epoch close, ledger reconciler converts deferred credits into either applied tokens (if used) or releases them to pool. Reconciliation tests will verify sum(deferred credits) + used_tokens == previous epoch allocations.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: reserved.capacity.micro_reset = off by default.
Phase 1 (Canary): Enable for internal test tenants and 3 low-risk customers. Monitor fairness-index and reconciliation logs for 3 billing cycles. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Selective opt-in): Allow customer opt-in via console + support toggle. Run reconciliation nightly jobs in audit mode (no billing changes) for 4 weeks.
Phase 3 (Default opt-in for new contracts): Offer as option during Dedicated onboarding; enable for older customers only after signed consent.
Phase 4 (Full rollout): Flip default and monitor churn. Gradual region-wise expansion.
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off at pool-level; micro-reset worker will stop granting new credits. Existing deferred credits remain in ledger and will reconcile normally at epoch end.
If a regression occurs (throttling increases >5% p95) revert immediately and run emergency reconciliation to refund customers affected (manual bill credits).
Postmortem and customer communications template in Confluence.
telemetry_checks: New metrics to add: reserved.micro_reset.granted (count+sum tokens), reserved.micro_reset.used, reserved.reservoir.size, pool.fairness_index (0-1).
Alerts: micro_reset.granted_rate > expected_baseline * 3 for >15m -> investigate leak or config bug.
Reconciliation alerts: nightly_reconciler.discrepancy_tokens > 0.1% of pool_capacity -> pager and automated snapshot for billing team.
Dashboards: per-pool time series for reservoir.size, throttle_rate, fallback_rate.
QA_checks: Unit tests for reservoir decay math and top-up caps. Edge tests for integer rounding of token grants.
Integration: spin up dedicated pool, synthetic tenant with scripted traffic around epoch boundary and validate no more than configured carryover budget is consumed.
Reconciliation test harness: simulate 1000 tenants with random usage patterns; assert per-tenant billed tokens equal ledger outputs after epoch-close.
estimated_savings: 10-18% per-token cost reduction for bursty sustained workloads (internal estimate, depends on workload distribution)
notes_for_billing_team: Ledger entries created for micro-reset grants must include audit fields: grant_id, pool_id, tenant_id, timestamp, amount, epoch_id. Billing reconciler must be extended to consume grant_id for proofs. Coordinate with billing-team@redwood.ai and include nightly dry-run results before any customer-visible billing changes.
